title: Eviction cushion and capacity pivot runbook for GPU surge events
creator: Lina Zhang
description:
Summary: After several recent hosted API capacity events where tenant queues grew and throttles cascaded, we need an operational playbook and code changes that reduce abrupt tenant ejections and improve recovery speed. This ticket creates an 'eviction cushion' (a soft-reserve that delays hard evictions during short transients), implements a capacity pivot policy to rapidly shift burst load to warm spare pools, and formalizes a runbook for on-call and SRE to coordinate automated and manual actions.

Problem statement: During GPU exhaustion incidents we observed aggressive hard-eviction heuristics that amplify queue oscillation and tenant impact. Autoscaler priming lag plus prefetches amplified sudden demand peaks. Current mitigations (soft-throttles and prewarm) are partial and require manual coordination.

Goals: 1) Reduce customer-visible errors by introducing a short, measurable eviction cushion that lets the autoscaler and priming logic attempt recovery before evicting most requests. 2) Add a capacity pivot controller that can shift a subset of bursty tenants to warm spare pools (cross-pool spillback) within a deterministic time bound. 3) Provide a concise on-call runbook with decision gates, dashboards, and actionable playbook steps so humans can intervene if automation fails.

Scope (what's in/out): In scope: admission controller changes to support eviction cushion, autoscaler feedback loop to respect cushion, controller to orchestrate pivot to spare pools, telemetry and dashboard improvements, and the on-call runbook. Out of scope: long-term multi-region redispatch, pricing/chargeback changes for spillback, and refactoring of the entire admission pipeline (to be covered in followups).
acceptance_criteria: Eviction cushion implemented in admission service and variably tunable per pool (config flag + runtime override)
Capacity pivot controller prototype that can migrate up to 10% of in-flight requests to a spare pool within 30s in lab tests
Dashboards updated with cushion state, pivot actions, and customer impact estimator
On-call runbook published in Confluence with step-by-step human escalation and rollback steps
Automated chaos test that injects a 2x burst and verifies >50% reduction in 5xxs vs baseline
action_items: Design eviction cushion semantics and default values (Lina) - finalize by 2026-03-12
Implement cushion flag in admission-service and expose metric (Marco) - branch: feat/eviction-cushion
Prototype capacity pivot controller that coordinates with autoscaler and routing (SRE: Raul) - include dry-run mode
Add telemetry: cushion_active, cushion_remaining_seconds, pivot_attempts_total, pivot_success_rate (Telemetry team)
Update Console dashboards and create an incident TL;DR panel (Console: Priya)
Author on-call runbook and circulate for review with Eng, SRE, and PM (Lina + Marco)
Run lab chaos experiments and record results in Playbook doc (QA + SRE)
Prepare canary rollout plan with feature gates and runtime kill-switch (Release Eng)
Post-deploy run 72-hour observation and collect token-level cost delta (Observability)
If cushion reduces 5xxs <50% in canary, escalate to rollback and begin follow-up investigation
comments: 2026-03-10 - Lina Zhang: Created ticket after postmortem call. Initial design doc sketched in Confluence. Want to avoid wide-sweeping eviction heuristics used previously.

2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented prototype flag and local metric emission. Dropped initial default cushion to 6s to reduce tail latency impact — needs tuning. Pushed branch feat/eviction-cushion for early review.

2026-03-12 - Raul Gonzalez (SRE): Built pivot controller prototype that does dry-run redirect of traffic to a spare pool. Observed ~20s mean redirect time in cluster with realistic priming — work needed to get below 30s SLA.
2026-03-13 - Priya Menon (Console): Added a temporary dashboard panel showing cushion state and pivot ops. Suggest adding a 'pivot risk' estimator to the TL;DR panel.

2026-03-13 - Security review note: no sensitive material. Confirmed pivot only routes requests to Redwood-managed spare pools and honors tenant isolation. Security OK to proceed pending standard deployment checklist.
2026-03-14 - Lina Zhang: Updated acceptance criteria to require chaos test. Scheduling canary for 2026-03-20 with 5% traffic envelope. Please add any extra KPIs to comments before 2026-03-16.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cushion could increase end-to-end latency for some steady-state requests. Mitigation: default cushion is small (6s) and per-pool tuning is enabled; telemetry to detect client tail latency regressions

Risk: Pivoting traffic to spare pools may cause cross-pool KV cache inefficiencies and transient quality regressions. Mitigation: restrict pivot to low-LLM-memory models first, enable canary fraction, and include model-compatibility oracle
Risk: Automation failure could delay evictions and overload spare pools. Mitigation: add runtime kill-switch and human-in-the-loop escalation steps in runbook
notes: Design tradeoffs considered: a) longer cushion improves recovery but increases tail latency b) short cushion reduces latency but may not give autoscaler time to prime c) pivoting reduces eviction but adds routing complexity

We prioritized short default cushion with aggressive telemetry and a pivot controller that is opt-in per pool. This gives predictable safety while allowing operations to enable stronger behavior for critical customers.
Suggested follow-ups after initial rollout: automated tenant scoring to decide eligibility for pivot, chargeback/onboarding changes, and long-term multi-region redispatch
